scope: The standing restored Thap Khwan court residence at Sanam Chandra Palace, including its four main teak halls, its four smaller corner pavilions, raised open timber deck, two front stairs and tiled roofs. The landscaped park and detached royal residences are outside this model.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: Four larger halls face inward, four small service buildings occupy the corners, and teak decks connect them around a chan tree. The 1983 restoration reconstructed the pavilions with ceramic tile in place of thatch and brick paving in the open undercroft.
Raised traditional timber house construction uses tapered walls, steep gables, teak frame-and-panel walls, and open undercrofts.
The written analysis partitions connected open deck, court and veranda, and identifies two front stair approaches. The court and gaps in the undercroft are kept open.
